DeepResearch Bench II: Diagnosing Deep Research Agents via Rubrics from Expert Report

paper.arxiv.2601.08536

Prepared 15 Nov 2026 · Evidence snapshot 12 Nov 2026 · Report research-2026-11-12.1 · Evidence research-2026-11-11.candidate.1

Evidence & scope

Complete primary manuscript and pinned creator README/LICENSE were independently read in three separate AI invocations, with exact author, source-verifier and adversarial source-content reviews for all 16 paper-scoped claims. Expert-report construction, human rubric quality controls, original paper and later repository model/judge/task protocols, missing-value uncertainty, source-reported agreement and per-task rights statements remain qualified. The work explicitly concerns DeepResearch Bench II. No identity equivalence or distinct-family admission is inferred for the separate generic DeepResearch Bench inventory target, which remains retained and unresolved. No full task/article payload, source code execution, experiment reproduction, comprehensive upstream rights clearance or current provider performance is asserted; core eligibility is not frozen.

Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

DeepResearch Bench II: Diagnosing Deep Research Agents via Rubrics from Expert Report · documents: The DeepResearch Bench II batch-size ablation uses ten human-labeled model reports in PDF, DOCX, Markdown and HTML formats; with Gemini 2.5 Pro judging 50 rubrics per batch, the paper reports 91.75% accuracy and F1 of 89.57.

candidate.next8.drbii.paper.batch-size-ablation-scope.v1

  • The reported average evaluation cost is $0.2513 per task in that study; a batch of ten has higher reported accuracy, 92.29%, but costs $0.4832 and has slightly lower F1, 89.37.
  • The authors select 50 for the observed cost/F1 balance; this small report sample does not establish universal judging accuracy or current evaluation pricing.
